al-lantern-parade-familiar-roads::Porchl.line: The porchlight flickered twice at ten
You said the rain was coming in
I moved the chairs away from the screen
And watched the street turn silver green
Leave one light on for the way back home
Leave one light on when the roads are gone
The storm can have the maple tree
It cannot take this room from me
Your coffee cooled beside the door
The weather radio asked for more
A neighbor knocked with muddy shoes
We made some space and shared the news
Leave one light on for the way back home
Leave one light on when the roads are gone
Across the dark a window shone
Then another answered from down the road
At morning's edge the rain let go
We counted every roof we know
Leave one light on for the way back home
And let the waking neighborhood glow

al-mira-solace-paper-hearts::Good in the.line: You call me brave when the lights are low
Then hurry out before the buses go
I know that coat, I know that sound
The second step that turns around
Are we still good in the morning?
When the coffee tells the truth
Are we still good in the morning?
When the sun comes looking for you
I left your keys beside the bread
And said the things I should have said
The kitchen clock refused to wait
We let the toast go dark on plates
Are we still good in the morning?
When the coffee tells the truth
Are we still good in the morning?
When the sun comes looking for you
No grand repair, no painted sky
Just stay and let me meet your eyes
We'll be good in the morning
If we can start with what is true

al-tarnished-crown-iron-vigil::The Broke.line: The outer wall gave way at dawn
Our iron banners dragged in mud
The king had fled through western stone
And left the gate to us alone
Hold fast, hold fast, the bridge is narrow
Hold fast until the horns are still
No crown can bind the hands that guard it
No oath can make a traitor kneel
We counted shadows in the breach
The captain's voice was nearly gone
He set his shield against the hinge
And told the wounded to move on
Hold fast, hold fast, the bridge is narrow
Hold fast until the horns are still
No crown can bind the hands that guard it
No oath can make a traitor kneel
At dusk we crossed the broken stones
With no bright standard left to raise
The city lived beyond the smoke
And knew the names of those who stayed

al-the-north-inlet-soundings::Keeper of.line: Old Mara climbs the headland stairs
With salt in every coat she wears
She checks the wick, she cleans the glass
And watches all the trawlers pass
Keep the light where the channel bends
Keep it burning for our friends
Out past the shoals and through the spray
There's still a lantern marking the way
A gale blew hard on Thursday night
The harbor vanished out of sight
Her grandson carried oil uphill
And found her at the window still
Keep the light where the channel bends
Keep it burning for our friends
A small boat answered through the foam
One steady flash to guide it home
At dawn the kettle started singing
Wet boots lined the kitchen floor
Mara said the lamp was simple
Then went to fill it once more

al-mosaic-ledger-common-ground::No Small.line: Mrs. Bell put a jar on the counter
Said the window needs a pane by winter
First kid dropped in three bent pennies
Next came a note from old Miss Jenny
No small change on this side of town
Every coin makes a little sound
Stack them high till the glass comes round
No small change on this side of town
Rico fixed the frame on Friday
Brought his tools on the late train highway
Told us how his dad once worked here
Bought him soup when the rent was unclear
No small change on this side of town
Every coin makes a little sound
Stack them high till the glass comes round
No small change on this side of town
Now you can see the corner in the morning
Bread in rows and the buses forming
She kept that jar beside the till
For whatever the next cold season will

al-alba-cordero-patio-adentro::La Silla.line: Queda una silla roja junto al balcón
La pintó mi madre con una canción
Lleva tres veranos mirando pasar
A los que se marchan hacia el mar
Ven, toma asiento, que empieza el calor
Trae tus historias y un poco de sol
La silla roja conoce tu voz
Y guarda un lugar para los dos
Hoy llegó mi hermano con pan y café
Habló del camino que quiere emprender
No le pedí promesas al partir
Le di la llave para volver aquí
Ven, toma asiento, que empieza el calor
Trae tus historias y un poco de sol
La silla roja conoce tu voz
Y guarda un lugar para los dos
Al caer la tarde la calle cambió
Sonó una guitarra desde otro balcón
Dejé la puerta abierta al anochecer
Por si alguien volvía buscando dónde ser

al-juniper-frame-handwritten-weather::Th.line: I found your letter under winter mail
A little rain had softened every edge
You drew the house with crooked windowpanes
And wrote about the seeds along the hedge
I'll write back before the garden wakes
Before the first green breaks the clay
There are words I held too long to say
I'll put them in an envelope today
The kettle clicked, the table shook
I read the last line one more time
You asked if I still kept the little book
Of every tree we meant to find
I'll write back before the garden wakes
Before the first green breaks the clay
There are words I held too long to say
I'll put them in an envelope today
The mail truck stopped beside the gate
I waved it down with ink still blue
The road can make a letter late
But now it knows the way to you

al-wren-duarte-little-victories::A Dance.line: We couldn't pay the band that year
The porch steps needed nails
You found a station playing slow
Between the weather and the sales
So take my hand beside the truck
We'll make a ballroom out of gravel
The neighbors might call it bad luck
I call it one more way to travel
Your good shirt had a coffee stain
My boots were full of yard
We stepped around the garden hose
And laughed when it got hard
So take my hand beside the truck
We'll make a ballroom out of gravel
The neighbors might call it bad luck
I call it one more way to travel
Next spring we'll fix that porch for sure
Tonight the stars can wait
We danced until the radio faded
And called the whole thing great

al-silas-ferre-silver-hours::Call When Y.line: Your bag is waiting by the stairs
The cab is warming up outside
We said enough to fill the room
Then stood in silence for a while
Call when you arrive
I want to hear the door behind you
Call when you arrive
No need to say what we might do
The driver taps the dashboard clock
I carry your old coat downstairs
You say the road is clear at night
I say the bridge is under repair
Call when you arrive
I want to hear the door behind you
Call when you arrive
A little sound will see me through
The taillights turn beyond the trees
I leave the hallway lamp alive
For all the things we couldn't settle
Call when you arrive

al-asha-venn-velvet-weather::The Air Cle.line: You put the groceries on the floor
And asked me what the silence meant
I watched the rain against the door
Trying to name where all the daylight went
But the air clears, the air clears
After we let the hard words through
The air clears, the air clears
And I can see the room with you
We found the ticket from that train
The one we missed in early spring
You laughed and said we'd missed worse things
I laughed before I knew I could
The air clears, the air clears
After we let the hard words through
The air clears, the air clears
And I can see the room with you
We put the cold food on the shelf
And opened up the kitchen blinds
No perfect sky above the street
Just enough blue to change our minds
